findings.evidence: openspec/specs/completion-lifecycle/spec.md:1482: "Finish SHALL run the independent review when `[independent_review] enabled = true` and then the shared finalize function ... Without that setting the review stays optional". The delta spec.md has no MODIFIED entry for it. Its new requirement says "`finish` SHALL launch no reviewer for any other change". The candidate updates the matching prose in docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md and openspec-workflow.md, but not this spec requirement.
findings.summary: The accepted requirement "Finish finalizes the change" is not modified by the delta, so it now contradicts the new rule. It still says finish runs the review whenever review is enabled. The delta says finish reviews only a risky change and launches no reviewer otherwise.

findings.evidence: design.md says `risky_paths(root, base_ref)`, `quick_review_dir(root)` and `git diff <merge-base>..HEAD`. The code has `risky_paths(root)`, which derives the base from `origin/<main_branch>` (template/scripts/independent_review.py), `quick_review_path` (task_content_identity.py) and `quick_path_partition`, which uses `{merge_base}...HEAD`.
findings.summary: design.md describes interfaces and a diff form that the implementation does not use. The design should be updated first, per the no-silent-divergence rule.

findings.evidence: tests/test_publication_recovery_cli.py install_scripts: the diff adds "independent_review.py" after "openspec_lifecycle.py", but the list already ends with "independent_review.py", "task_content_identity.py".
findings.summary: The candidate adds `independent_review.py` to a copy list that already contained it, so it now appears twice. The copy is harmless but redundant.
